solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Presume the setter's improving

parts.note: to posit is to assume or presume
the setter's means 'the setter has', from the setter's point of view I have, so I'VE

explanation.surface: A setter boasts that they are getting better, taking it for granted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the setter's' reads as a possessive but is 'the setter has', which the setter would write as I'VE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something constructive and helpful can be called positive, as in a good influence that makes things better.

clue.text: Two characters talked about card game

indicators.note: talked about means the clue words are spoken and heard

parts.note: two letters, P and K, which said together make the game's name

explanation.surface: Two people gossip about a game of cards.
explanation.walkthrough: The French card game is pronounced 'pee-KAY', like the letters P and K.
explanation.definitionFit: Piquet is an old two-player trick-taking card game played with a 32-card pack.

clue.text: Bizarre soccer war alarming one in field

indicators.note: bizarre means strange, so the letters are put into an odd new order

explanation.surface: A strange war over football breaks out on the pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'field' suggests a football pitch, but it is a farmer's field where birds are frightened off.
explanation.definitionFit: A figure stuffed with straw stands among crops to frighten away birds.

clue.text: Increasingly seedy gallery, not quite on the level

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above what follows
not quite means falling short of the full word, so the last letter goes

parts.note: the Tate is the London art gallery
a tier is a level or layer

explanation.surface: An art gallery becomes shabbier and not entirely honest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the level' reads as honest, but 'on' is the down-clue signal for placing one piece above the next; 'not quite' clips the Tate, London's national gallery of British art.
explanation.definitionFit: Tatty means shabby or worn, and the comparative form means more run-down.

clue.text: Limit such as priest set up

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means the letters are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: e.g. means for example, such as
Rev is short for Reverend, a priest's title

explanation.surface: A boundary is established, as by a clergyman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' turns EGREV round to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A verge is an edge or border, the point at which something is about to happen.

clue.text: One bowl, gold-rimmed, sent from East in perfect state

indicators.note: in an across clue, sent from the east means read from right to left, backwards
gold-rimmed means gold forms the rim around what is mentioned with it

parts.note: AU is the chemical symbol for gold
one is the Roman numeral I
a pot is a bowl or round vessel

explanation.surface: A gilded bowl shipped from the Orient sounds like a perfect treasure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rimmed' puts IPOT inside AU, giving AIPOTU, which 'sent from East' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas More's imaginary island gave its name to any ideal society or flawless condition.

clue.text: Vehicle turned up in motor club trading centre

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: the RAC is the Royal Automobile Club, a British motoring organisation
a mart is a market

explanation.surface: A car arrives at a motoring club's market.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reverses RACMART; the RAC is a British motoring association like the AAA.
explanation.definitionFit: A tramcar is a single carriage of a tram, a passenger vehicle running on rails in the street.

clue.text: Reward what eavesdropper does on phone

indicators.note: on phone means as heard down a telephone line, so the word is spoken

parts.note: an eavesdropper pries into others' business

explanation.surface: A snooper listens in on a call to collect a payment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on phone' seems part of the eavesdropping scene but is the homophone signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A prize is something given as a reward for winning or merit.

clue.text: Finesse is lacked by satirist that's bungled lines

indicators.note: is lacked by means the letters of is are missing from satirist
bungled means messed up, so the remaining letters are rearranged

parts.note: RY is the abbreviation for railway, railway lines

explanation.surface: A satirist with poor technique botches his verses.
explanation.walkthrough: SATIRIST without the letters of IS leaves SATRIT, rearranged by 'bungled' as ARTIST.
explanation.definitionFit: Artistry is skill and delicacy of execution, just as finesse is refined skill.

clue.text: Dramatist defending women's case for settlement in lawless US

indicators.note: defending means surrounding and protecting, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: Oscar Wilde was the Irish playwright
W is the abbreviation for women

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outside, its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A playwright stands up for women in a legal claim about a frontier town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' looks like a legal case but means the outer letters of 'settlement'.
explanation.definitionFit: The American frontier in the 19th century was famous for its outlaws and rough justice.

clue.text: Contestant at late stage put up hand, nursing broken nail

parts.note: to quarter troops is to lodge or put them up

indicators.note: nursing means holding close, so one piece holds the other inside it

parts.note: a fist is a clenched hand

indicators.note: broken signals the letters of nail are rearranged

explanation.surface: A competitor deep into a tournament raises a hand while protecting a damaged fingernail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' is to lodge someone, not to raise; 'broken' rearranges the nail, and 'nursing' holds the result inside the hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A player who has reached the round of the last eight is a competitor near the end of the event.

clue.text: Lament in verse is tragedienne's last on English stage

parts.note: a leg is a stage of a journey or race

indicators.note: last points to the final letter of the word tragedienne's

explanation.surface: A tragic actress performs a mournful poem on an English stage.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces come in a different order from the clue: E, LEG, IS, then the final letter of 'tragedienne's'.
explanation.definitionFit: To write an elegy is to mourn someone in a poem, the verb form of that mournful poem.

clue.text: Author's daughter revolts, first son having left

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter in family trees

indicators.note: the first son here means the first S, of the two in the word, has gone

parts.note: something that revolts you sickens you

explanation.surface: A novelist's daughter rebels once her eldest brother has moved out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolts' is a verb meaning disgusts, not rebels as the surface suggests; dropping the opening S of SICKENS leaves ICKENS.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Dickens is the Victorian novelist of Oliver Twist and Great Expectations.

clue.text: Temporarily stop working for crook

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of
a crook is a rogue or villain

explanation.surface: Someone suspends their work on behalf of a criminal.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition takes in 'working', so only 'for crook' is wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Parliament is prorogued when its sitting is suspended without being dissolved, a temporary halt to its business.

clue.text: Going early, seconds having withdrawn on tiptoe?

indicators.note: seconds are the second letters of each word, and they have been taken away

explanation.surface: Leaving early, a boxer's corner men slip away quietly.
explanation.walkthrough: The second letters of 'Going' and 'early' are O and A; removing them leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Walking on tiptoe is one way of moving with great care and caution, hence the question mark.

clue.text: From time to time Ernie swears he's stopped lying

indicators.note: from time to time means taking only every other letter of Ernie swears

explanation.surface: Ernie occasionally insists that he has given up telling lies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lying' looks like dishonesty but means lying down: someone who gets up out of bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A riser is a person who gets up from bed, as in an early riser, so has ceased being horizontal.

clue.text: Small number of challengers fight where serviceman might retreat

parts.note: the entry for a competition is the number of contestants
to box is to fight with fists

explanation.surface: A handful of challengers fight where a soldier might pull back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreat' is shelter, not withdrawal from battle.
explanation.definitionFit: A guard on duty can step into this small hut for shelter from the weather.

clue.text: Eclipses elated pundits claiming last of credit

parts.note: up means in high spirits

indicators.note: claiming means taking in, so the pundits hold the extra letter

parts.note: sages are wise authorities, pundits

indicators.note: last of points to the final letter of credit

explanation.surface: Jubilant experts take the credit and outshine others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'claiming' puts the final letter of 'credit' inside the pundits.
explanation.definitionFit: To upstage someone is to steal attention from them, outshining them as an eclipse blots out the sun.

clue.text: Muscle man in debt, but only just?

parts.note: P is a penny, the smallest sum one could owe, so the debt is only just a debt
someone who owes is, playfully, an ower

explanation.surface: A strongman is barely solvent, owing almost nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags an invented word: one who owes is an OWER, and owing just P, a penny, means scarcely in debt.
explanation.definitionFit: Muscle means strength or force, as in political or financial clout.

clue.text: BBC chief gets heads of broadcasting in readiness for current revival

indicators.note: for means in place of, one letter swapped out for others

parts.note: Lord Reith was the first Director-General of the BBC
I is the symbol for electric current

indicators.note: heads of points to the first letter of each of the three words

explanation.surface: The BBC's boss prepares broadcasting for a fresh revival.
explanation.walkthrough: In REITH, BIR replaces I to give the answer; 'gets' is a link. John Reith founded the BBC's public-service ethos.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebirth is a renewal or renaissance, something coming back to life.

clue.text: Pointing out one effect of cold on turning 100

indicators.note: on means placed after, the cold effect following the turned hundred
turning means the word for a hundred is read backwards

parts.note: a ton is slang for a hundred
icing, ice forming on surfaces, is one result of freezing weather

explanation.surface: Someone remarks on a frost effect after a dial turns to a hundred.
explanation.walkthrough: TON, slang for 100, read backwards by 'turning' gives NOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Noticing can mean remarking on or drawing attention to, as when a reviewer points something out.

clue.text: Take part, fixing favourite in advance

indicators.note: fixing means setting firmly, here one piece set into another
in shows where the favourite is placed

parts.note: to come is to advance, approach
a pet is a favourite

explanation.surface: Someone takes part in rigging a race for the favourite beforehand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fixing' and 'in advance' read as race-rigging, but 'advance' is COME, which holds PET.
explanation.definitionFit: To compete is to enter a contest and take part in it.

clue.text: Doctored tax system embraced by Southern Democrat

indicators.note: embraced by means held inside the other letters

parts.note: PAYE is Pay As You Earn, the British income tax system

explanation.surface: A tax scheme is rigged by a Democrat from the South.
explanation.walkthrough: PAYE is the British system of taking income tax from wages before they are paid.
explanation.definitionFit: To doctor an animal is a euphemism for neutering it, and spaying is the female version.

clue.text: All but one of team fit and sound

parts.note: a football or cricket team has eleven players, and one fewer than eleven is ten
fit means capable, able to do something

explanation.surface: Every player save one is healthy and in good condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'team' stands for eleven, the size of a cricket or football side, so all but one is ten.
explanation.definitionFit: A sound argument is one that can be defended or maintained, which is what a tenable position is.

clue.text: Fighter contributing to disruption in jail

indicators.note: contributing to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A fighter helps cause unrest inside a prison.
explanation.definitionFit: A ninja is a Japanese warrior trained in stealth and martial arts.

clue.text: Sweet that can cause greater exposure of teeth?

definitions.text: Sweet that can cause greater exposure of teeth?

parts.words: Sweet that can cause greater exposure of teeth?
parts.note: a sugary chewy candy, read whimsically as a fall in gum level, receding gums showing more tooth

explanation.surface: A dental warning about a confectionery that bares more of your teeth.
explanation.walkthrough: The sweet's name, split, describes gums dropping and so revealing more tooth.
explanation.definitionFit: This chewy jelly sweet is a standard confection, and the split name describes receding gums.

clue.text: Device supplied by medic to US army?

indicators.note: to means attached to, the medic coming after

parts.note: GIs are American soldiers, loosely the army
MO is a medical officer

explanation.surface: A doctor issues a gadget to American troops.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that GIs are soldiers rather than the army itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A gismo, also spelt gizmo, is a gadget or contraption.

clue.text: High church court set German's eyeballs rolling

indicators.note: eyeballs rolling suggests the letters of the phrase tumbling into a new order

explanation.surface: A senior church tribunal makes a German roll his eyes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set' is a link word; the letters of 'German's eyeballs' are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: In Presbyterian churches such as the Church of Scotland, the supreme governing and judicial body has this name.

clue.text: Hit man finds bandage

parts.note: to swat is to hit sharply
he is the pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: A hitman discovers a dressing for a wound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hit man' reads as an assassin but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To swathe is to wrap or bind in cloth, as a bandage is wound round an injury.

clue.text: Suit has hole in it? Times editor gobsmacked

indicators.note: has here means holds or contains, so the suit takes another piece
in it says the hole goes inside the suit rather than beside it

parts.note: a plea is a suit or action in law
O, a round letter, stands for a hole
X is the multiplication sign for times

explanation.surface: An editor at the Times is astonished at a suit full of holes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suit' is a lawsuit, not clothing: PLEA with O inside gives POLEA.
explanation.definitionFit: Being pole-axed, felled as if by a butcher's axe, is a vivid idiom for being utterly stunned.
